beats.trigger: A hundred tiny agents cost more to coordinate than they save.

beats.trigger: If one agent can produce what you need, use one.

take_homes: Default to one agent. Split only when the pieces need different access, different dialects or genuinely different stances, and use the 'could one prompt do this?' test on anyone proposing more.
Failures happen at the handoffs between agents, and the audit does not check whether the result is true. The doubt stays open and I say so.
Splitting by access gives me the way into the employee-data conversation: which agent may see what, and a human gate where it matters.

monday.move: Ask my HR business partner and the DPO what employee data an agent may touch, then sketch my weekly people-metrics summary as one agent that proposes and never sends.
monday.who: Me, one HR partner, and the DPO
monday.when: Tuesday, after my leadership team meeting
monday.stop_condition: The DPO or works council says employee data can't go in the tool yet.
monday.blocker: I haven't asked the works council or DPO, and without them I can't use real employee data.

misconception.why: Nothing in the module mentioned roles, headcount or who does the work. 'Split by access' gave me a question for the DPO, but I still think agents take headcount first and I don't know which roles.

one_line: Useful rule of thumb to use one agent unless you have a real reason, and honest about what it can't check, but it never says what any of this means for the people doing the work.
